attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his reply section of the exchange.

semantics.note: Three-part observation. 'Apparently' qualifies only the malware part, and the proposition keeps it. 'With CNET using it' ties CNET to ChatGPT.

contract.note: In the sentence, 'it' plainly refers to ChatGPT, so reading it as 'CNET used ChatGPT' is the ordinary reading, not a stretch. Taking it to mean generic AI text tools would be generous to the speaker. The result turns on this reading.

evidence.note: Dated before the post. Reputable coverage of Check Point's finding that criminals used ChatGPT to build malware.
Dated before the post. Reports that CNET's AI-written stories contained errors. It does not name the tool.
CNET's editor-in-chief says the tool was an in-house AI engine, not ChatGPT. This is a company disclosure, but it is direct evidence of which tool was used. Published before the evaluation date.
CNET admits that several AI-assisted stories needed corrections, some of them substantial. That backs the error part.

reviews.rationale: The malware part holds: Check Point reported ChatGPT-assisted malware before the post. The errors part holds: CNET's AI stories needed corrections. The claim that CNET used ChatGPT fails: CNET says the engine was in-house, not ChatGPT. Two of the three parts hold and the tool attribution is contradicted.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words. In context, 'we don't yet' means we do not yet have AGI by his stated definition.

semantics.note: The short fragment is correctly expanded from context into a claim about the state of AI at the post date.

contract.note: The plain reading (no AI met his AGI definition as of January 2023) is the ordinary reading, and the period tied to the post date is reasonable.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own launch post, inside the target period, admits ChatGPT gave incorrect or nonsensical answers. It is a company disclosure, but it admits limits rather than promoting the product.
December 2022 report of the OpenAI CEO saying ChatGPT was not reliable for factual answers.
February 2023, after the target period. OpenAI still treats AGI as not yet created.

reviews.rationale: Inside the period, the developer of the most prominent system admitted basic reliability failures well below human level. The packet has no credible claim that any system met Marcus's AGI definition in January 2023.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words, given as his view ('What I think').

semantics.note: The proposition drops the 'I think' framing. The statement is a research diagnosis of what AGI needs, not a checkable fact about the world.

contract.note: The contract rightly declines a literal reading that such databases do not exist. Without a theory of what AGI requires, there is no test for necessity or sufficiency.

evidence.note: A 2020 Google disclosure shows a large structured knowledge base already existed. That bears only on a literal reading of 'missing', not on whether it is adequate for AGI.

reviews.rationale: The claim is an opinion-framed diagnosis of the ingredients AGI lacks. Neither the needed 'ideas' nor the required knowledge coverage is specified, so no evidence could settle it. Large knowledge graphs existed, but that does not test his point about adequacy.
